# Nicomachean Ethics

Aristotle. *Nicomachean Ethics*. Translated by W. D. Ross. [Internet Classics Archive witness](https://classics.mit.edu/Aristotle/nicomachaen.5.v.html). Selected sections read on 8 September 2026: V.3–5. The host identifies the translator; this receipt does not identify or collate a specific printed edition, Greek text or full work.

The selected account **sources** [the historical branch](../../../../etymologies/apportionment-and-economy/HISTORICAL-BRANCHES.md) and **qualifies** its [whole-field](../../../../etymologies/apportionment-and-economy/WHOLE-FIELD.md). The historical proposition and Taylor’s relational operation retain distinct authority.

## Selected passages

<a id="aristotle-nicomachean-ethics-ross-q001"></a>
### q001 — Distribution and rectification

**Paraphrase:** Distribution compares persons and shares through proportion under a criterion of merit that political orders dispute. Rectification instead treats the parties equally in respect of injury and restores a mean between gain and loss. The passage distinguishes these offices rather than supplying one universal arithmetic rule for every allocation.

**Locator:** V.3–4.

**Verification:** selected W. D. Ross online translation read; paraphrase-ready, no print or Greek collation and no exact quotation claim.

<a id="aristotle-nicomachean-ethics-ross-q002"></a>
### q002 — Exchange, demand and conventional money

**Paraphrase:** The builder and shoemaker bring unlike products into proportion for reciprocal exchange. Money represents demand by convention; users can alter it or render it useless. Aristotle qualifies commensurability: goods so different are not strictly commensurable, but become sufficiently comparable relative to demand. This is his philosophical treatment, not independently verified coinage history.

**Locator:** V.5.

**Verification:** selected W. D. Ross online translation read; paraphrase-ready, no print or Greek collation and no exact quotation claim.
